question.problem: Using the standard form of the Maclaurin series of $\frac{1}{1-x},$ find the first three non-zero terms of the series expansion of the definite integral ${\int }_{0}^{1/2}\frac{1}{1-2{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x.$
question.worked_solution:
The power series expansion of $\frac{1}{1-x}$ is given by 

$$
\frac{1}{1-x}=1+x+{x}^{2}+⋯.
$$

Replacing $x$ with $2{x}^{3}$ in the above, we get

$$
\frac{1}{1-2{x}^{3}}=1+2{x}^{3}+4{x}^{6}+⋯.
$$

Finally, we calculate the definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1/2}\frac{1}{1-2{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{1/2}(1+2{x}^{3}+4{x}^{6}+⋯)\text{d}x \\  & =(x+\frac{{x}^{4}}{2}+\frac{4{x}^{7}}{7}+…){|}_{0}^{1/2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{32}+\frac{1}{224}+⋯\end{aligned}
$$
